question: Can technique 'deg' lower a live SHA3 row at r7, and where is it dead?
number: FES on chi7-input cone (268 planes, degree 16 in the 40-dim 2-round-affine field): 51.3 FES + 41.2 setup + 3.3 explicit + 14.32 transpose + 6 probe + 0.515 = 116.6 ops/msg -> 123.969 at n=40 vs live 124.73447 (-0.765 bit); n>=60: 75.5 ops -> 123.341 (-1.39). Break-even n=37.5. Cube test (full 1600-bit state after round 6, 6 cubes each): dim 15 and 16 nonzero 6/6, dim 17 and 18 zero 0/6+0/4 -> degree exactly 16, so round 7 needs D=16.
notes: Same model as sha3r6/lowdegree (3D+1 FES step, setup C(n,<=D)); eval cost scaled R/6, unit 271*R, N=2^127.993. Premise carried from the r6 filing e641788b which was REFUTED on success-probability space (fresh coins), not on degree: an r7 build must give the search fresh algorithmic coins. Also H_coset and memory (derivative tables) premises open. D=16 chain not run end to end.

question: Can technique 'lin' lower a live SHA3 row at r7 to 24, and where is it dead?
number: Rounds 1-2 affine structure is already inside the live LS1 line (round-0 linear stage 162 ops of 35,517 per step at r7). The residual lever is a 3-round structure: rank<=2 in 210 runs and exhaustive 6-bit transition check (r6 evidence, rounds 1-3 only), ceiling 12.5 ops/msg = 0.13 bit of a 138.7 ops/eval step, likely 0. Prefix rounds 1-3 do not depend on R, so the finding carries to every R>=6.

question: Can technique 'trail' lower a live SHA3 row at r7 to 24, and where is it dead?
number: Needs a 5-round (r7) to 22-round differential trail after a 2-round connector. r6 evidence: 2-round connector leaves 5 DF, 3-round is >=33 DF short, best published 4-round trail weight 141 floors the cost near 2^132 > 2^128 birthday; each extra round only adds weight (a longer trail contains a 4-round sub-trail). Cost >= 2^132 for all R>=7.
notes: DEAD r7..r24 as a collision route. Lower bound uses best published weight (141), not a proved minimum; a lighter 4-round trail would reopen r6/r7 only.
